_README: #703 — THE RECONCILIATION RATCHET. The floor a run's common-law carry must not fall below.
WHAT IT RECORDS: what the contract CURRENTLY ACHIEVES, not what anyone hopes it achieves. It is
seeded from a real delivered run, never from a fixture, because a floor invented at a desk ratchets
against nothing. driver/test/commonlaw-carry-ratchet.test.mjs compares and reports.
RATES, NOT ABSOLUTES: runs differ in size, and a run that retrieves twice as much while reconciling
the same share has not regressed. Each rate carries the counts it came from so a reader can check the
arithmetic rather than trust a percentage.
A TRIP ANNOTATES, NEVER SUPPRESSES: the deliverable ships first. Below-floor means the ROUND cannot
claim the contract held; it never means a client gets nothing.
MOVING IT UP IS THE POINT. When the seat-compliance work lands (the judgment half of #703 — why the
seat writes rows for 13% of cells when the dictation says one per cell), re-seed from the round that
proves the improvement and record which run did it. A wave that ends with these numbers unmoved is a
finding for the handover, not a footnote. Lowering the floor requires the same: a named run and a
reason, in this file, where the next reader will see it.
RATES ARE TRUNCATED DOWNWARD, never rounded to nearest. Seeded at 0.133562 the cells floor sat ABOVE
the 39/292 it was seeded from and tripped on its own measurement — the always-fires mode the ruling
refused, arriving through a rounding choice rather than a design one. The test asserts a floor can
never exceed the counts it claims to come from.
PER-CLASS FLOORS are deliberately NOT here yet. If these rates prove noisy across scenario classes,
that is a later refinement on R2/R6 data — one global floor seeded from one round is honest about
what it knows; five invented per-class floors would not be.
